candidates.current_role: State Representative, Texas House District 75, since 2013
candidates.background: Gonzalez was raised in Clint and has represented House District 75 in eastern El Paso County since winning election in 2012. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin, a master's degree from St. Edward's University, and a doctorate in curriculum and instruction from UT Austin. Her House biography says she is vice chair of the House Appropriations Committee and works as executive director of MASBA: School Board Members for Latino Equity.

priorities.text: Says her work is grounded in strengthening public schools, expanding economic opportunity, supporting agriculture, and making sure rural and border communities are not overlooked.
Says she has authored bills to improve public schools, increase economic development, and support agriculture in the district.

record.text: Voted against SB 2 (2025), which created a $1 billion education savings account program for private school and homeschool costs; it passed the House 86 to 61.

Voted for Amendment No. 22 to the 2026-2027 budget (April 2025), which would have directed the state to seek a federal waiver to expand Medicaid eligibility; it failed 63 to 85.

priorities.text: Her House biography highlights legislation on COVID relief for small businesses, prescription contraception access, economic development incentives, and workforce programs.
